findings.title: Backup-code login skips the password when any totpCode is sent
findings.body: Password verification runs only when credentials.totpCode is empty (line 121). The new branch then accepts a matching backup code and never checks the TOTP value. A caller who knows the email and one backup code can therefore sign in with no password by also sending any non-empty totpCode (for example "000000"). The UI copy and the login form still treat the backup code as a replacement for the authenticator only, after the password step, so this is an account takeover path if a backup code leaks (downloaded file, clipboard, setup response). Require a valid password for CAL users on the backup-code path, and do not let a dummy totpCode bypass that check.

findings.title: Backup codes are compared case-sensitively
findings.body: Codes are 10 hex characters (0-9a-f) and the login UI placeholder is "XXXXX-XXXXX", which leads users and mobile keyboards to enter uppercase. Matching uses indexOf on the raw string after only stripping dashes, so "AAAAA-AAAAA" does not match "aaaaa-aaaaa". The same check in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts (line 61) has the same bug. Legitimate backup codes will be rejected at login and when disabling 2FA. Normalize by lowercasing (and trimming) before compare.

findings.title: A backup code can be redeemed twice under concurrent logins
findings.body: Consumption is a read-modify-write: decrypt the list, indexOf the code, set that slot to null, then update. Two overlapping authorize calls can both observe the same unused code and both return a session before either write lands. The product promise is that each code works exactly once. The update needs to be conditional (transaction or compare-and-swap on the stored ciphertext) so a code that was already removed cannot authorize a second session.

findings.title: Lost-access toggle submits the disable form
findings.body: The Lost access / Go back control is a Button inside the disable Form with no type="button" and no preventDefault. A button's default type is submit, so clicking it both flips the backup-code view and posts whatever is currently in the password/TOTP/backup fields. That can disable 2FA accidentally, or fail the request and show an incorrect-code error, instead of only switching inputs. Set type="button" (same issue on the download control in EnableTwoFactorModal, which sits inside the enable Form and will also submit handleEnable).

findings.title: Enable-2FA login test never leaves the backup-code step
findings.body: After a successful OTP, EnableTwoFactorModal now stays open on the backup-code step and only calls onEnable when backup-codes-close is clicked. This test still waits for the security-page switch and asserts it is checked without closing that dialog. The second test was updated to click close; this one was not, so it will fail or pass only because of the existing isChecked() quirk noted in the FIXME. It also never exercises login or disable with a backup code (the new TODO), so the feature this PR adds is untested.

findings.title: Missing-backup-codes message points at a settings action that does not exist
findings.body: missing_backup_codes tells the user to generate codes in settings. This PR only creates codes during 2FA setup and clears them on disable; there is no regenerate control. Users who enabled 2FA before the migration have backupCodes null and will see this error on Lost access, with no way to follow the instruction except fully disabling and re-enabling 2FA. The string should describe that actual path.
